name: Patagonia (Torres del Paine)
description: Dramatic granite towers, glaciers, and multi-day treks at the southern tip of the Andes.

name: Dolomites
description: Jagged limestone peaks with via ferrata routes, alpine huts, and Tyrolean cuisine.

name: Zermatt & the Swiss Alps
description: Classic alpine village beneath the Matterhorn, equally suited to hiking and skiing.

name: Triglav National Park
description: Slovenia's only national park — turquoise alpine lakes ringed by the Julian Alps.

name: Tatra Mountains
description: Central Europe's highest range — sharp peaks and glacial lakes with far fewer crowds than the Alps.

name: Tian Shan Range
description: Remote 'heavenly mountains' with horseback trekking routes and yurt-stay villages.

name: Banff National Park
description: Turquoise glacial lakes and the Canadian Rockies, easily accessible by car.

name: Annapurna Region
description: Legendary Himalayan trekking circuit through villages, rice terraces, and high passes.

name: Maldives
description: Overwater bungalows on coral atolls — the archetypal luxury beach escape.

name: Bora Bora
description: A volcanic peak ringed by a turquoise lagoon and coral reef.

name: El Nido, Palawan
description: Limestone karsts rising from hidden lagoons and island-hopping boat tours.

name: Turks and Caicos
description: Powder-white Grace Bay Beach with calm, shallow turquoise water.

name: Zanzibar
description: Spice-island beaches paired with Stone Town's Swahili-Arab old city.

name: Raja Ampat
description: Remote archipelago with the richest marine biodiversity on earth.

name: Seychelles
description: Granite boulders and palm-backed beaches across a scattered island chain.

name: Ko Lipe
description: A small, laid-back island with no cars and reef-lined beaches.

name: Everest Base Camp Trek
description: The classic high-altitude trek to the foot of the world's tallest mountain.

name: Antarctic Peninsula
description: Expedition-cruise access to icebergs, penguin colonies, and untouched wilderness.

name: Skeleton Coast
description: Fog-shrouded shipwreck coastline where the desert meets the Atlantic.

name: Faroe Islands
description: Dramatic sea cliffs, waterfalls, and turf-roofed villages between Iceland and Norway.

name: Svalbard
description: Polar bear territory in the high Arctic — glaciers, fjords, and the midnight sun.

name: Greenland Ice Sheet
description: Vast ice sheet and iceberg-filled fjords accessible from small coastal towns.

name: Ala Archa Gorge
description: A dramatic canyon gateway into the Tian Shan, popular for day treks and climbing.

name: Danakil Depression
description: One of the hottest, lowest places on Earth — active volcanoes and technicolor sulfur springs.

name: Pacific Coast Highway
description: Cliffside highway from San Francisco to Los Angeles via Big Sur.

name: Iceland Ring Road
description: A full loop of Iceland — waterfalls, glaciers, volcanoes, and black-sand beaches.

name: Utah's Mighty Five
description: A driving loop through five national parks of red-rock desert scenery.

name: Great Ocean Road
description: Coastal drive past limestone sea stacks and rainforest detours.

name: Garden Route
description: Coastal route through forests, lagoons, and wildlife reserves.

name: Transfăgărășan Highway
description: A dramatic switchback mountain road through the Carpathians.

name: Ring of Kerry
description: A coastal loop through Atlantic villages, cliffs, and green hills.

name: Karakoram Highway
description: One of the world's highest paved roads, cutting through the Karakoram range.

name: Kyoto
description: Centuries of temples, gardens, and tradition woven into a living city.

name: Rome
description: Ancient ruins, Renaissance art, and everyday life layered across one city.

name: Petra
description: A rose-red city carved into desert canyon walls by the Nabataeans.

name: Luang Prabang
description: Gilded temples and monk processions along the Mekong River.

name: Fez
description: The world's largest car-free urban area — a maze of medieval medina alleys.

name: Cusco & Sacred Valley
description: Inca capital and gateway to Machu Picchu, set high in the Andes.

name: Bagan
description: Thousands of ancient temples scattered across a plain, best seen at sunrise.

name: Matera
description: Ancient cave-dwelling city carved into limestone ravines.

name: Oaxaca
description: Mexico's culinary capital — mole, mezcal, and vibrant market culture.

name: Lyon
description: France's gastronomic capital, known for traditional bouchon restaurants.

name: Bangkok
description: World-class street food alongside temples and a buzzing urban core.

name: San Sebastián
description: Michelin-starred pintxos culture on a Basque coastal city beach.

name: Bologna
description: Italy's food capital — birthplace of ragù, tortellini, and porticoed streets.

name: Hoi An
description: A lantern-lit ancient trading port famous for its street food scene.

name: Penang
description: A hawker-food capital blending Malay, Chinese, and Indian culinary traditions.

name: Chengdu
description: Fiery Sichuan cuisine and giant pandas in a laid-back teahouse city.

name: Tokyo
description: A hyper-modern megacity with pockets of quiet tradition around every corner.

name: Lisbon
description: Hilly, tile-covered streets over the Tagus River with strong café culture.

name: Copenhagen
description: Bike-friendly design capital with a strong food and wellness scene.

name: Mexico City
description: Sprawling capital layering Aztec ruins, colonial architecture, and world-class food.

name: Seoul
description: Palaces and night markets alongside a fast, design-forward modern city.

name: Buenos Aires
description: European-flavored boulevards with tango, steakhouses, and late-night culture.

name: Porto
description: Port-wine cellars along the Douro River beneath tiled riverside houses.

name: Tbilisi
description: A hilly old city of sulfur bathhouses, wine bars, and Soviet-era architecture.

name: Serengeti
description: Endless plains hosting the annual wildebeest migration.

name: Galápagos Islands
description: Isolated volcanic islands where wildlife shows no fear of visitors.

name: Kruger National Park
description: One of Africa's largest game reserves, reliable for Big Five sightings.

name: Amazon Rainforest (Ecuador)
description: Dense jungle lodges offering close encounters with rainforest biodiversity.

name: Pantanal
description: The world's largest tropical wetland — the best place on earth to spot jaguars.

name: Yellowstone National Park
description: Geysers, hot springs, and abundant wildlife in America's first national park.

name: Madagascar
description: An isolated island of lemurs, baobabs, and ecosystems found nowhere else.

name: Borneo Rainforest
description: Ancient rainforest home to orangutans and river-based jungle lodges.

name: Salar de Uyuni
description: The world's largest salt flat at 10,000 square kilometers, transforming into a perfect mirror in the rainy season when a thin layer of water reflects an unbroken sky. In the dry season the geometric hexagonal salt tiles and cactus-studded islands create a surreal otherworldly landscape.

name: Cappadocia
description: A volcanic landscape of fairy-chimney rock formations, ancient cave churches, and 2,000-year-old underground cities in central Turkey. Hot air balloon rides at sunrise over the surreal rose-colored valleys are among the most iconic travel experiences in the world.

name: Socotra
description: A remote Yemeni archipelago so isolated it evolved in complete biological separation, producing alien-looking dragon blood trees, cucumber trees, and endemic species found nowhere else. Often called the Galápagos of the Indian Ocean.

name: Zhangjiajie
description: Towering sandstone pillars that inspired the floating mountains in Avatar.

name: Lençóis Maranhenses
description: White sand dunes filled with rainwater lagoons that appear only part of the year.

name: Pamukkale
description: A ridge of brilliant white calcium carbonate terraces forming natural warm-water pools above the ancient Roman city of Hierapolis in western Turkey. Visitors wade barefoot through warm mineral pools surrounded by 2,000 years of history.

name: Sossusvlei & Deadvlei
description: Towering red dunes surrounding a bone-white clay pan of ancient dead trees.

name: Danxia Landform
description: Rainbow-striped sandstone mountains formed over millions of years.

name: Ubud, Bali
description: Rice terraces, yoga retreats, and a slower pace inland from Bali's beaches.

name: Azores
description: Volcanic Atlantic islands with crater lakes, hot springs, and green pastures.

name: Kerala Backwaters
description: Slow houseboat cruising through palm-lined canals and lagoons.

name: Iya Valley
description: A remote mountain valley of vine bridges and hot spring ryokans, rarely visited by tourists.

name: Sedona
description: Red-rock desert scenery paired with a strong wellness and spa culture.

name: Tuscany Countryside
description: Rolling vineyard hills, farmhouse stays, and slow, food-centered days.

name: Ikaria
description: A Blue Zone island known for longevity, unhurried village life, and hot springs.

name: Nosara
description: A jungle-meets-beach town built around yoga, surfing, and slow mornings.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Japan's highest peak at 3,776 m — a near-perfect stratovolcano sacred to Shinto and visible from Tokyo on clear days. The two-month summer climbing season draws 200,000+ hikers, most arriving at night to catch the Goraiko sunrise from the summit crater.

name: Mount Nyiragongo
description: One of Africa's most active volcanoes, holding the world's largest permanent lava lake — a churning 200-meter cauldron visible after a 6-hour ridge hike from Goma. Overnight stays in ranger huts at the crater rim offer a mesmerizing and humbling spectacle.

name: Mount Bromo
region: East Java, Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park
description: Indonesia's most photographed volcano — a stark smoking cone in the Tengger Caldera that produces Southeast Asia's great pre-dawn jeep-and-sunrise tableau from Penanjakan viewpoint. The active crater is a short walk across volcanic sand and up steep steps.

name: Popocatépetl
description: Mexico's iconic 5,426 m smoking volcano paired with Iztaccíhuatl — continuously active since 1994, its exclusion zone fluctuates with eruption cycles. Best experienced from viewpoints near Puebla or Paso de Cortés, the saddle between the two volcanoes.

name: Chimborazo
description: At 6,263 m the farthest point from Earth's center due to the equatorial bulge, Chimborazo towers over Riobamba on Ecuador's Avenue of Volcanoes. The Whymper route ascends glaciers to the Veintimilla summit; a shorter approach reaches the Cara Norte hut at 5,000 m for non-technical acclimatization.

name: Mount Kenya
description: Africa's second highest mountain at 5,199 m, with glaciated rock spires rising from equatorial rainforest and moorland populated by giant lobelias, groundsel trees, and elephants. Point Lenana (4,985 m) is reached by trekkers; the twin main peaks require technical climbing.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Africa's highest peak at 5,895 m — an immense free-standing volcano rising from the Tanzanian savanna whose glacier-capped summit is reachable without technical skills via the Lemosho or Marangu routes. Success depends on careful acclimatization over 6-8 days.

name: Mount Etna
description: Europe's largest and most active volcano at up to 3,357 m, erupting in some form almost continuously and shaping Sicilian civilization for millennia. A cable car and 4x4 take visitors to 2,800 m; guided hikes reach the summit craters on calm days for views over the Ionian coast.

name: Merapi
description: The world's most consistently active volcano looms over royal Yogyakarta, erupting frequently with pyroclastic flows visible from Prambanan and Borobudur. Pre-dawn guided hikes launch from Selo for sunrise crater views; jeep tours through the 2010 lahar zone show the scale of recent devastation.

name: Mount Rainier
description: A 4,392 m active stratovolcano dominating the Seattle skyline and cloaked in more glacier ice than any other peak in the contiguous US. Wildflower meadows at Paradise and Sunrise are among the finest subalpine landscapes in North America; the summit requires a two-day guided technical climb.

name: Stromboli
description: The 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean' — a small inhabited Aeolian island volcano that has erupted almost continuously for 2,000 years. Evening guided hikes to the 924 m summit crater watch Strombolian eruptions loft molten bombs into the night sky above the sea.

name: Damavand
description: Asia's highest volcano at 5,610 m — Iran's highest peak and a cultural symbol appearing in Persian epic poetry for 3,000 years, looming over Tehran through the Alborz range. Non-technical but demanding; summit day involves sulfurous fumaroles and severe altitude effects near the crater.

name: Cotopaxi
description: One of the world's highest active volcanoes at 5,897 m — a near-perfect snow cone on Ecuador's Avenue of Volcanoes, reopened for guided glacier ascents after eruptions in 2015. The high-altitude páramo on its lower flanks is accessible to cyclists and hikers well below the snowline.

name: Teide
description: Spain's highest peak at 3,718 m and the world's third tallest volcanic structure measured from its ocean base, rising above a UNESCO World Heritage lava field on Tenerife. A cable car reaches 3,555 m; a separate summit permit is required for the final trail to the top.
activities: stargazing (one of Europe's finest dark sky sites)

name: Mount Vesuvius
description: The only active volcano on mainland Europe, famous for burying Pompeii and Herculaneum in 79 CE. A paved path winds through lava fields to the 300-meter deep crater rim, with sweeping views over the Bay of Naples and the cities spread across its base.

name: Rinjani
description: Lombok's dominant 3,726 m volcano encircles a crater lake (Segara Anak) and an active inner cone that erupts periodically. The 2-3 day summit trek crosses volcanic rock, dense forest, and ridge lines before rewarding climbers with one of Southeast Asia's most dramatic calderas.

name: Mount Elbrus
description: Europe's highest peak at 5,642 m (by the continental divide definition) — a dormant twin-peaked stratovolcano in the Caucasus accessible by gondola to 3,800 m. The standard south-side route involves guided glacier travel and 5-7 days for acclimatization and ascent.

name: Mauna Kea
description: Hawaii's dormant shield volcano and the world's tallest mountain from base to summit at 9,330 m total (4,207 m above sea level), home to the world's largest astronomical observatory complex. The Visitor Information Station at 2,800 m offers some of the finest stargazing accessible by car anywhere on Earth.

name: Puncak Jaya
description: Oceania's highest peak at 4,884 m and the last equatorial glaciers in the Pacific, requiring a helicopter approach from Timika and a complex Indonesian permit process. As the Seven Summits' most logistically demanding peak, it combines technical rock and ice climbing with extreme remoteness in the Papuan highlands.

name: Manaslu
description: The world's eighth highest peak anchors the Manaslu Circuit — a 14-17 day restricted-area trek through Gurung villages, deep gorges, and over the 5,106 m Larkya La pass. Far less trafficked than the Annapurna or Everest circuits with comparable Himalayan scenery.
activities: Birendra Tal glacier lake day hike
Nubri and Tsum ethnic village visits

name: Ama Dablam
description: Widely considered the most beautiful mountain in the Himalayas — its distinctive hanging glacier and spire-like 6,812 m form visible from the entire Everest Base Camp trail above Namche Bazaar. Technical mixed rock and ice climbing at altitude makes it a serious objective for experienced alpinists.

name: Vinson Massif
description: Antarctica's highest peak at 4,892 m and the most remote of the Seven Summits, reachable only by ski-equipped aircraft from Punta Arenas via the ALE Union Glacier camp. The climb is non-technical by Seven Summits standards but extreme cold, 24-hour sunlight, and total remoteness make it a profound undertaking.

name: Eiger
description: The 3,967 m Eiger's North Face — the Nordwand — is one of the most storied objectives in alpine climbing, dropping 1,800 m of vertical limestone and ice above Grindelwald, and claimed dozens of lives before its 1938 first ascent. Non-climbers approach via Kleine Scheidegg viewpoint or the Jungfraujoch railway.

name: Kanchenjunga
description: The world's third highest mountain at 8,586 m, straddling the Nepal-Sikkim border and accessible via one of Nepal's most remote and rewarding treks through rhododendron forests, glacier moraines, and high yak pastures to both north and south base camps. One of the least visited major Himalayan trek routes.

name: Ben Nevis
description: Britain's highest peak at 1,345 m, a plateau summit above Fort William holding snow year-round on its shadowed north face. The Mountain Track is a well-maintained but relentless 17 km roundtrip with 1,340 m of elevation gain; the Carn Mòr Dearg Arête offers a more dramatic horseshoe ridge route.

name: Mount Fitz Roy
description: Patagonia's most recognizable granite spire — 3,405 m needles rising above El Chaltén and photographed at alpenglow from Laguna de los Tres. The 4-5 hour day hike from El Chaltén is achievable for most fit hikers; the technical summit is among Patagonia's most coveted alpine objectives.
activities: Laguna de los Tres day hike

name: Nanga Parbat
description: The world's ninth highest peak at 8,126 m — the 'Naked Mountain' — with the Rupal Face, the tallest mountain wall on Earth at 4,500 m. Fairy Meadows, a pastoral plateau at 3,300 m with unobstructed views, is accessible by jeep and short hike from Raikot Bridge.

name: Mount Athos
description: A self-governing Orthodox monastic community on a remote Greek peninsula continuously inhabited since the 10th century — 20 monasteries cling to cliffs above the Aegean with Byzantine icon collections inaccessible to women. Access for men requires a special permit (diamonitirion), only 110 visitors allowed daily.

name: Mount Robson
description: The 'Monarch of the Canadian Rockies' and BC's highest peak at 3,954 m, perpetually cisted in cloud and storms. The Berg Lake Trail (23 km each way) is one of Canada's most scenic backcountry routes, passing turquoise Berg Lake under the mountain's colossal ice-cliff north face.
activities: Berg Lake camping below glacier face

name: Mount Ararat
description: Turkey's highest peak at 5,137 m — the dormant volcano of biblical Noah's Ark fame rising above the Anatolian plain near the Armenian border. Guided 4-5 day ascents cross alpine meadows and a permanent snowfield; the mountain is visible on clear days from Yerevan.

name: Matterhorn
description: The 4,478 m pyramid-shaped peak above Zermatt is the most recognized mountain on Earth — its four-sided form a symbol of the Alps since the 1865 first ascent tragedy. The Hörnli Ridge is climbed by 2,000-3,000 guided parties per season; Zermatt's Gornergrat railway brings everyone else to outstanding viewpoints.

name: K2
description: The world's second highest mountain at 8,611 m — widely considered the most dangerous of the 8,000 m peaks, with a summit-to-death ratio exceeding Everest. The Baltoro Glacier approach trek via Concordia is one of the world's great high-altitude treks, passing the full Karakoram concentration of 8,000 m peaks.
activities: K2 Base Camp trek via Baltoro Glacier
Broad Peak Base Camp side trip

name: Mount Kazbek
description: Georgia's 5,054 m dominant Caucasus volcano towering above the Kazbegi valley on the Georgian Military Highway. The Gergeti Trinity Church perched on a spur below the glacier is one of the Caucasus's most iconic viewpoints; the summit glacier route is achievable in 2 days from the Meteo Hut.
activities: Kazbek Meteo Hut base camp trek

name: Mount Roraima
description: A prehistoric 2,810 m sandstone tepui at the Venezuela-Brazil-Guyana triple border — an ancient plateau ecosystem that inspired The Lost World, with endemic carnivorous plants, black crystal formations, and species found nowhere else. The 6-day trek via Paraitepui is the only non-technical route.
activities: El Foso waterfall on tepui plateau

name: Grand Teton
description: Wyoming's defining 4,199 m granite peak rises abruptly from the Jackson Hole valley floor — one of the most dramatic mountain fronts in North America. The Exum Ridge is a classic technical alpine climb; Jenny Lake and Cascade Canyon offer accessible day hikes beneath the Teton skyline.

name: Mont Blanc
description: Western Europe's highest peak at 4,808 m straddling the French-Italian border above Chamonix — the birthplace of alpinism. The Goûter Route summit requires 2 days via the Nid d'Aigle train and glaciers; the Aiguille du Midi cable car gives non-climbers extraordinary high-alpine access at 3,842 m.
activities: Aiguille du Midi cable car (3,842 m)

name: Zugspitze
description: Germany's highest peak at 2,962 m, accessible by two cable car routes from Garmisch-Partenkirchen with views spanning 400 km to four countries on clear days. In summer the summit sits above the remnant Zugspitzplatt glacier; in winter it anchors a reliable ski area.

name: Mount Olympus
description: Greece's highest peak at 2,917 m and ancient home of the Twelve Olympian Gods — the world's oldest formally protected mountain. A marked trail from Litochoro rises through dense forest and gorges to Refuge A hut; the Mytikas summit involves a short but exposed scramble.
activities: Litochoro to Refuge A trail hike

name: Scafell Pike
description: England's highest peak at 978 m in the Lake District — the hardest and most rewarding leg of the Three Peaks Challenge. The Corridor Route from Seathwaite crosses boulder fields and ridges above Wastwater; the summit cairn surveys the full Lake District on clear days.
activities: Three Peaks Challenge (Ben Nevis, Scafell Pike, Snowdon)
Wastwater approach walk (deepest lake in England)

name: Adam's Peak
description: A 2,243 m sacred peak venerated by four religions — pilgrims climb 5,500 illuminated steps from midnight to catch sunrise and the mountain's perfect triangular shadow projected onto the clouds below. The footprint at the summit chapel is claimed as Buddha's, Shiva's, Adam's, and St. Thomas's, depending on faith.
activities: sunrise and shadow viewing from summit

name: Aiguille du Midi
description: A 3,842 m granite needle above Chamonix accessible by the world's highest vertical-gain cable car, with a glass-floored 'Step into the Void' box at eye-level with Mont Blanc's summit. The Vallée Blanche off-piste ski descent and Cosmiques Ridge technical climb both originate from this station.
activities: cable car summit + Step into the Void

name: Grossglockner
description: Austria's highest peak at 3,798 m in Hohe Tauern National Park, reached via the Grossglockner High Alpine Road — one of Europe's most scenic drives cresting 2,571 m with glacier views. The summit requires a guided technical ascent over the Pasterze Glacier.

name: Huascarán
description: Peru's highest peak at 6,768 m in the Cordillera Blanca — a technical two-summit glacier climb approached through Huaraz. The surrounding national park contains 600+ km of trails, including the celebrated Laguna 69 day hike to a turquoise lake beneath hanging glaciers.
activities: Callejón de Huaylas valley scenic driving

name: Aconcagua
description: The highest peak outside Asia at 6,961 m — 'The Stone Sentinel' dominating the Andes above Mendoza. The Normal Route via Plaza de Mulas base camp is non-technical but demands 2-3 weeks of acclimatization; it's the most popular high-altitude mountaineering objective in the Americas.
activities: Normal Route guided ascent (Plaza de Mulas base)

name: Table Mountain
description: The 1,085 m flat-topped sandstone massif defining Cape Town's skyline — one of the New Seven Wonders of Nature, accessible by rotating aerial cable car or 350+ hiking routes. On clear days the summit reveals 360° views over the Cape Peninsula, Table Bay, and the Winelands.

name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
description: New Zealand's highest peak at 3,724 m and a sacred ancestor in Māori cosmology, rising above the Mackenzie Basin amid New Zealand's largest glaciers. The Hooker Valley Track is the country's finest accessible valley walk; the technical summit requires a serious alpine commitment.
activities: Lake Tekapo dark sky stargazing combination

name: Mount Whitney
description: The highest peak in the contiguous United States at 4,421 m, achievable as a 22 km day hike via the Main Trail from Whitney Portal — with the most competitive permit lottery in US wilderness. The final granite ridge walk above Trail Camp offers sweeping Sierra Nevada views down both sides of the range.
activities: Main Trail day hike (permit lottery required)
overnight Trail Camp and summit day
Lone Pine film history town visit

name: Mount Sinai
description: The 2,285 m peak in the Sinai Peninsula where Moses is said to have received the Ten Commandments — sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Pilgrims climb 3,750 steps by torchlight before dawn to reach the summit chapel for one of the Middle East's most celebrated sunrises.

name: Snowdonia
description: Wales's highest peak at 1,085 m (Y Wyddfa) anchoring a national park of lakes, cwms, and volcanic ridges. Snowdon attracts one million+ visitors per year across six routes; the Crib Goch knife-edge arête is one of the UK's most dramatic mountain ridges.
activities: Pyg Track or Llanberis Path summit hike

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
description: Colorado's premier mountain park — 415,000 acres with 77 peaks above 4,267 m and Trail Ridge Road, the highest continuous paved road in the US at 3,713 m. Tundra wildflower meadows, herds of valley elk, and the technical Longs Peak define a complete Colorado mountain experience.
activities: Trail Ridge Road alpine scenic drive
Bear Lake trail system day hikes

name: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park
description: A UNESCO World Heritage canyon park in the Spanish Pyrenees — the Ordesa Valley is one of Europe's finest glacial canyons, ringed by 3,000 m limestone walls and waterfalls. Monte Perdido at 3,355 m and the nearby Cirque de Gavarnie across the French border give the Pyrenees at their most dramatic.

name: Jasper National Park
description: Canada's largest Rocky Mountain park — wilder and less visited than Banff, with the Icefields Parkway cutting through its core. Elk herds roam into Jasper townsite at dusk, the Maligne Lake boat tour accesses Spirit Island, and the Athabasca Glacier is a short walk from the highway.
activities: Maligne Lake Spirit Island boat tour

name: Cairngorms National Park
description: The UK's largest national park — a sub-arctic plateau holding four of Britain's five highest peaks and one of its last ancient Caledonian pine forests. In winter it's Scotland's main ski area; in summer the high plateau offers arctic-like tundra walking with red squirrels and ospreys in the glens below.
activities: Ben Macdui summit hike (highest in Cairngorms)

name: Denali National Park and Preserve
description: Alaska's premier wilderness park dominated by Denali (6,190 m) — North America's highest peak — accessed by a single road with mandatory bus reservations. Wonder Lake delivers the full Alaska Range reflection; grizzly bears, wolves, and caribou roam the open tundra visible from the bus.
activities: park bus wilderness tour to Wonder Lake
grizzly bear and wolf wildlife watching

name: Fiordland National Park
description: New Zealand's most dramatic national park — a UNESCO World Heritage wilderness of towering fiords, ancient beech forest, and snowfields. Milford Sound and Doubtful Sound offer boat cruises beneath 1,200 m sheer rock walls; the Milford Track is often called the finest walk in the world.

name: Hohe Tauern National Park
description: Central Europe's largest national park — 1,800 km² of the Austrian Alps anchored by the Grossglockner High Alpine Road and the Krimml Waterfalls, Europe's tallest. Golden eagles, ibex, and chamois inhabit the high ridges above glacier valleys and alpine meadows.

name: Mount Kosciuszko
description: Australia's highest peak at 2,228 m — a gentle boardwalk walk from the Thredbo chairlift through alpine meadow and snow gum woodland to a rounded summit with 360° views. The uniquely Australian sub-alpine flora blooms in summer; Thredbo and Perisher ski resorts operate on the surrounding slopes in winter.
activities: summit boardwalk walk via Thredbo chairlift

name: Mount Logan
description: Canada's highest peak at 5,959 m and the largest mountain massif in North America — an immense ice-covered summit in the remote Yukon requiring a ski-plane approach into Kluane National Park. Technical glacier expeditions take 2-3 weeks; the peak sees fewer than 100 attempts per year.
activities: ski-plane approach to King Col base camp

name: Perito Moreno Glacier
region: Santa Cruz Province, Los Glaciares National Park
description: One of the world's few advancing glaciers — a 5 km wide, 60 m high wall of fractured blue ice that calves thunderously into Lago Argentino near El Calafate. Multi-level walkways bring visitors face-to-face with the ice face; guided crampon trekking is available on the glacier surface.
activities: ice trekking with crampons (mini or full trek)
Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers boat excursion

name: Aletsch Glacier
description: The longest glacier in the Alps at 23 km — a UNESCO World Heritage ice stream flowing from the Jungfrau massif. The Aletsch Arena viewpoints at Bettmerhorn and Eggishorn are reached by cable car; guided summer ice walks traverse the glacier surface with views of the Matterhorn and Weisshorn.

name: Franz Josef Glacier
region: West Coast, Westland Tai Poutini National Park
description: A rapidly retreating West Coast glacier descending from the Southern Alps into temperate rainforest — one of the world's few glaciers accessible within walking distance of sea-level jungle. Helicopter ice hikes land on the upper glacier; guided walks explore the lower terminal ice and moraines.
activities: glacier valley floor walk to terminal face

name: Jungfraujoch
description: The 'Top of Europe' — a railway station at 3,454 m reached by the highest railway in Europe through tunnels bored into the Eiger and Mönch. The Sphinx Observatory deck, Ice Palace, and Aletsch Glacier panorama draw 500,000+ visitors a year as a day trip from Interlaken or Grindelwald.

name: Mer de Glace
description: France's largest glacier at 12 km — a river of cracked blue ice beneath the Grandes Jorasses, reached by the historic Montenvers rack railway from Chamonix. The ice cave carved into the glacier each summer exposes ancient blue walls; retreating 30 m per year, it's a visible record of climate change.

name: Vatnajökull
description: Europe's largest glacier at 8,100 km² — a vast ice cap covering 8% of Iceland, with outlet glaciers descending to black sand beaches and its own sub-glacial volcanic system. Winter reveals vivid blue crystal ice caves; summer opens cramponed glacier hiking from Skaftafell and boat tours of Jökulsárlón lagoon.

name: Snæfellsjökull
description: The 1,446 m glacier-capped volcano at the tip of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — Jules Verne's entry point to Journey to the Center of the Earth, with mystical lava tubes, sea caves, and bird cliffs in the surrounding national park. Snowcat tours reach the glacier summit; the peninsula is a self-contained Iceland highlight.

name: Hindu Kush
description: An 800 km range spanning Afghanistan and Pakistan — one of Central Asia's last great unexplored trekking regions, with peaks rising to 7,708 m (Tirich Mir) through ancient silk road passes and remote Chitrali and Nuristani cultures. Access from Chitral, Pakistan is far more practical than from Afghanistan.
activities: Tirich Mir Base Camp trek (Chitral, Pakistan)

name: Pamir Mountains
description: The 'Roof of the World' — a high-altitude plateau averaging 4,000 m in Tajikistan, with the Wakhan Corridor offering trekking through remote Pamiri and Afghan Wakhi villages. The M41 Pamir Highway between Osh and Dushanbe is one of the world's great mountain road journeys.

name: Pyrenees
description: A 430 km natural border between France and Spain — a compact range with Andorra nestled inside, offering the GR10 and GR11 long-distance trails, Ordesa Canyon, and ski resorts. Each Pyrenean valley has its own distinct French or Spanish character, from Basque coast to Catalan foothills.
activities: Ordesa y Monte Perdido day hiking

name: Atlas Mountains
description: North Africa's highest range — dominated by Jebel Toubkal at 4,167 m, the highest peak in the Arab world and North Africa. Berber village trekking through walnut-terraced valleys from the Imlil trailhead makes for a distinctive combination of high-altitude scenery and living mountain culture.

name: Scottish Highlands
description: A vast sweep of glacially-carved mountains, lochs, and moorland covering the northern third of Scotland — 282 Munros (peaks over 914 m) form the backbone of Scottish hill walking culture. Glen Coe, Torridon, and the Cuillin Ridge of Skye are among Europe's finest mountain landscapes.
activities: Glen Coe scenic drive and walks
Loch Ness and Great Glen driving

name: Sierra Nevada
description: California's 650 km granite spine — containing Yosemite, Kings Canyon, Sequoia, and Tahoe, and traversed by the 340 km John Muir Trail. The High Sierra combines granite domes, emerald lakes, giant sequoias, and 4,000 m passes into the definitive American mountain range.

name: Caucasus Mountains
description: A 1,200 km range forming the land bridge between the Black and Caspian Seas — containing Europe's highest peak (Elbrus, 5,642 m) and Georgia's dramatic Kazbegi and Svaneti valleys. Ancient watchtower villages, living Caucasian cultures, and trekking through Mestia and Tusheti define the Georgian side.

name: Julian Alps
description: Slovenia's compact alpine heartland — Triglav National Park protects the highest peak in the former Yugoslavia at 2,864 m, above the emerald Soča River valley and Lake Bled. Glacier-carved ridges, azure karst rivers, and medieval towns pack extraordinary variety into a small area.

name: Rwenzori Mountains
description: The 'Mountains of the Moon' on the Uganda-DRC border — an equatorial range of glaciers, giant heather forests, and otherworldly vegetation zones. The 7-day Rwenzori circuit reaches Margherita Peak at 5,109 m, Africa's third highest, through a landscape that Darwin described as unlike anything on Earth.
activities: giant heather and lobelia forest walk
Kasese base town and access logistics

name: Drakensberg
description: South Africa's 'Dragon Mountains' — a 1,000 km basalt escarpment rising to 3,482 m on the Lesotho border. The Royal Natal NP's Amphitheatre cliff face is one of the world's great rock walls; hundreds of San Bushmen rock art caves preserve Africa's oldest continuous artistic tradition.
activities: Tugela Falls hike (world's second tallest waterfall)
San Bushmen rock art cave visits

name: Alps
description: The 1,200 km arc of mountains spanning eight countries from the French Riviera to Vienna — the Alps contain the highest peaks in Western Europe, over 100 ski resorts, and villages like Zermatt, Chamonix, and Cortina that define mountain travel. Hiking, skiing, and rail journeys through the range are all world-class.
activities: Glacier Express and Bernina Express rail journeys
Swiss / French / Italian ski resort ski season

name: Himalayas
description: The world's highest mountain range — a 2,400 km arc containing all 14 eight-thousanders and shaping the climate of an entire continent. Nepal's trekking circuits (Everest, Annapurna, Manaslu) are the definitive high-altitude trail network; the range also holds Bhutan's sacred peaks and Tibet's monastery routes.

name: Andes
description: The world's longest continental mountain range at 7,000 km — running the full length of South America from Venezuela to Tierra del Fuego. The range holds Aconcagua (6,961 m), the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu, Patagonia's granite towers, the Bolivian altiplano, and Ecuador's Avenue of Volcanoes.
activities: Patagonia W-Trek and Torres del Paine (Chile)
Bolivia altiplano and salt flat tour
Ecuador Avenue of Volcanoes road journey

name: Ural Mountains
description: A 2,500 km range forming the traditional boundary between Europe and Asia — a modest but ancient range whose highest peak, Narodnaya (1,895 m), offers tundra hiking through relatively unknown wilderness. The southern Urals around Chelyabinsk and the northern Urals near Perm are the most accessible trekking areas.
activities: Narodnaya Peak summit hike (highest in Urals)
Siberian taiga and tundra wildlife walks

name: Carpathians
description: A 1,500 km arc of forested mountains sweeping through Romania, Slovakia, and Poland — Europe's last great old-growth forest belt and home to the continent's largest brown bear, wolf, and lynx populations. Romania's Fagaras Range and Transylvania combine medieval castles with wild Carpathian ridge walking.
activities: Transylvania castle and medieval village tour
Bucegi Plateau day hike near Brasov

name: Lake Hillier
description: A bubblegum-pink saline lake on Middle Island visible only by scenic flight or boat tour, its permanent color produced by Dunaliella salina algae and halophilic bacteria in the hypersaline water.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring
description: The largest hot spring in the United States, with vivid rings of orange and yellow microbial mats surrounding a deep sapphire center inside Yellowstone National Park. Best viewed from the short overlook trail above the boardwalk.

name: Spotted Lake
description: A sacred Okanagan First Nations site where mineral-rich water evaporates each summer to reveal dozens of large, distinctly colored circular pools in yellow, green, and blue. Viewed from the roadside in the Okanagan Valley wine country.

name: Lake Natron
description: A caustic alkaline lake in northern Tanzania whose extreme pH and heat create a vivid red-pink surface and calcify animals that touch the water. Home to one of Africa's largest flamingo breeding grounds, backed by the active Ol Doinyo Lengai volcano.

name: Darvaza Gas Crater
description: Known as the Door to Hell, a 69-meter-wide crater in the Karakum Desert that has burned continuously since a Soviet drilling rig collapsed in 1971. Most spectacular at night when the flames illuminate the surrounding desert for kilometers.

name: Zhangye Danxia
description: Layered formations of red, orange, yellow, and green sandstone spread across the Qilian Mountains, resembling a vast abstract painting. Colors are most vivid at sunrise and sunset, viewed from a series of well-maintained platforms.

name: Chocolate Hills
description: Over 1,200 nearly identical cone-shaped limestone hills spread across 50 square kilometers of Bohol island, turning chocolate brown in the dry season. Combine with the nearby Philippine tarsier sanctuary and Loboc River cruise for a full day.

name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
description: Thousands of towering quartzite sandstone pillars draped in vegetation that inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains in Avatar. Glass walkways, Asia's longest cable car, and vertiginous viewing platforms make this one of China's most dramatic landscapes.

name: Deadvlei
description: A dried white clay pan in Namibia where 900-year-old blackened camel thorn trees stand against towering red dunes under a cloudless sky. The stark contrast of black, white, and red against blue makes it one of the world's most photographed desert landscapes.

name: Richat Structure
description: A 50-kilometer-wide multi-ringed geological dome visible from space, known as the Eye of the Sahara. Concentric rings of ancient eroded rock in Mauritania's Adrar Plateau, reachable only by 4x4 expedition through remote desert.

name: Tianzi Mountain
description: A highland massif of quartzite sandstone pillars within the Zhangjiajie area, often draped in mist and cloud that amplifies the otherworldly atmosphere. A cable car provides access to summit viewpoints with 360-degree views over the stone forest.

name: El Tatio
description: The world's highest active geyser field at 4,320 meters above sea level, with over 80 geysers erupting most powerfully in the pre-dawn cold. Stay for the natural hot springs as the Atacama sun rises over the surrounding Andes peaks.

name: Fly Geyser
description: An accidental geyser in the Nevada desert created by a 1964 drilling error, now encrusted with vivid red and green mineral terraces that grow a few centimeters per year. Accessible only on guided tours run by the Burning Man nonprofit.

name: Wai-O-Tapu
description: A geothermal wonderland near Rotorua where champagne pools, sulfur lakes, and the daily Lady Knox Geyser create a landscape of vivid yellows and greens from dissolved gold, arsenic, and carbon dioxide deposits.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: A geothermal spa in an Icelandic lava field maintained at 38-39°C year-round. The milky-blue silica-rich water is famous for softening skin, while winter visits combine soaking with the possibility of Northern Lights overhead.

name: Dallol
description: The world's lowest land volcano and hottest inhabited place on Earth, with an alien landscape of acid pools, salt pillars, and multicolored sulfur fields in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression. The crystalline formations of yellow, green, and orange look like no other place on Earth.

name: Lake Toba
description: The world's largest volcanic lake, formed 74,000 years ago by a supervolcanic eruption that nearly caused a human extinction event. Today a serene caldera ringed by Batak villages, with the island of Samosir at its center offering traditional culture and tranquil lake life.

name: Askja
description: A remote caldera in Iceland's central highlands containing the milky-blue Víti crater lake, where Apollo astronauts trained before the Moon landing. F-road access requires a 4x4 and limits visitors to summer, making this one of Iceland's most desolate and authentic destinations.

name: Kelimutu National Park
description: A volcano on Flores island with three crater lakes that periodically shift color — from turquoise to rust-brown to black — driven by changing volcanic mineral chemistry. A 30-minute sunrise summit walk rewards with three strikingly different lakes lit by dawn.

name: Son Doong Cave
description: The world's largest known cave, containing its own jungle, river, and clouds inside Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park. Entry is strictly limited to roughly 1,000 permits per year, making this multi-day expedition one of the most exclusive wilderness experiences on Earth.

name: Fingal's Cave
description: A sea cave on the uninhabited island of Staffa formed entirely of interlocking hexagonal basalt columns, accessible only by boat from the Isle of Mull. The cathedral-like interior resonates with the sea and inspired Mendelssohn's Hebrides Overture.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
description: Limestone caves in New Zealand's Waikato region illuminated by thousands of bioluminescent glowworms that create a living starscape over underground rivers. A black-water rafting adventure runs through the same cave system for the more adventurous.

name: Valle de la Luna
description: A surreal landscape of salt flats, sand dunes, and sculpted rock formations in the Los Flamencos National Reserve near San Pedro de Atacama. At sunset the formations glow in gold, red, and orange against one of the darkest stargazing skies on Earth.

name: White Sands National Park
description: The world's largest gypsum dunefield — 710 square kilometers of blinding white sand in the Tularosa Basin of New Mexico. Sunrise and sunset turn the dunes pink and violet, and the boardwalks and backcountry trails offer solitude just hours from Albuquerque.

name: Abraham Lake
description: A reservoir in the Canadian Rockies famous for its frozen methane bubbles — trapped beneath the ice in winter, they stack into ethereal pillars visible from the shore. Access is easy along Highway 11 through the David Thompson Corridor.

name: Caño Cristales
description: Known as the River of Five Colors or the Liquid Rainbow, a remote Colombian river that turns vivid red, yellow, green, blue, and black from July to November due to the aquatic plant Macarenia clavigera blooming under clear shallow water. Requires a flight to La Macarena.
activities: hiking in Serranía de la Macarena

name: Strokkur
description: Iceland's most reliable geyser, erupting a 15-30 meter column of boiling water every 6-10 minutes in the Haukadalur geothermal area. Part of the Golden Circle route and easy to combine with Þingvellir and Gullfoss for a classic Iceland day.

name: Great Geysir
description: The original geyser after which all others are named, located steps from Strokkur in the Haukadalur valley. Though rarely active today, the surrounding geothermal area with its boiling hot springs and fumaroles remains a remarkable sight on Iceland's Golden Circle.

name: Makgadikgadi Pans
description: One of the world's largest salt flats, transformed in the wet season into a shallow lake attracting the world's largest flamingo and zebra migrations. In the dry season, the vast white expanse offers an almost meditative emptiness under African skies.

name: Salar de Atacama
description: South America's largest salt flat and one of the world's richest lithium deposits, ringed by snow-capped volcanoes and home to three species of flamingo that feed in the bordering lagoons. A 30-minute drive from San Pedro de Atacama.

name: Boiling Lake
description: The world's second-largest boiling lake, a flooded fumarole in Dominica's rainforest that bubbles and steams at near-boiling temperature. Reaching it requires a strenuous 8-hour round-trip hike through the Valley of Desolation — sulfur fields, hot springs, and dense jungle.

name: Cueva de los Verdes
description: A 6-kilometer lava tube created by a volcanic eruption 3,000 years ago, extending from the volcanic cone to beneath the Atlantic Ocean. The dramatic illuminated interior includes an auditorium used for concerts, plus a famous optical illusion that surprises every visitor.

name: Lökbatan Mud Volcano
description: One of the world's most dramatic mud volcanoes on the Absheron Peninsula near Baku, periodically erupting cool grey mud — sometimes dramatically with fire if natural gas ignites. Azerbaijan has more mud volcanoes than any other country in the world.
activities: combination with Yanar Dag fire mountain
